id_and_class.summary: Dan Zahavi argues that every conscious experience is given to its subject as ‘for me’, without any extra act of introspection or reflection. This pre-reflective self-awareness, which he calls for-me-ness, belongs to how experience is lived, and it constitutes a minimal self. A theory that leaves it out has explained something other than consciousness.

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is intrinsically self-conscious: each experience manifests itself to its subject in a first-personal way, and this for-me-ness is what makes it an experience at all.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Zahavi brackets the metaphysics. He holds that some forms of naturalized phenomenology are defensible and others are category mistakes, and that phenomenology can approach the hard problem by contesting the split between intentionality and phenomenality.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed. Zahavi treats for-me-ness as a primitive, non-relational feature of experience itself, without a claim about how experience arises from matter.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Experience is directed at objects (a tree, a melody) while being tacitly lived as one's own. Subjectivity is this non-objectifying self-presence, which comes before reflection, concepts, and autobiography.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: For-me-ness is a feature of how content is given, not an extra quale beside color or pain. Two qualitatively identical experiences in different subjects remain two because each carries its own first-personal givenness.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Experiences with first-personal character; a minimal, experiential self identical with that character. No Cartesian ego, soul, or self-object behind experience.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Phenomenological description of lived experience, plus structured clinical interviews such as the Examination of Anomalous Self-Experience (EASE).
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Layers of selfhood: the minimal self (pure mineness of experience) underlies richer bodily, temporal, affective, interpersonal, and narrative selves, which presuppose it.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; pre-reflective self-awareness; minimal selfhood; individuation of experiential lives.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Self-manifestation: experience is given to itself directly, without a second act that takes it as an object.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Zahavi's account concerns structure, not function. The minimal self is the basis on which reflection, narrative identity, and social selfhood build.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity of an experiential life comes from shared first-personal givenness, not from shared content.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Zahavi rejects representational and higher-order accounts in which self-awareness is a relation to an inner object.
core_claims_and_evidence: If awareness of an experience required a separate higher-order act, that act would need its own higher-order act, launching an infinite regress.
In the Mick and Mack thought experiment, two subjects with qualitatively identical experiences of a white wall still have distinct experiences, so for-me-ness individuates without adding content.
Richer narrative and social selves presuppose a minimal experiential self.

With Josef Parnas and Louis Sass, Zahavi developed the ipseity-disturbance model of schizophrenia as a disorder of the minimal self (hyperreflexivity and diminished self-affection), backed by two decades of EASE studies.
Thought insertion in schizophrenia reflects disturbed for-me-ness, not a loss of ownership.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological analysis and conceptual argument, supported by clinical psychopathology.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: The Examination of Anomalous Self-Experience (EASE), a 57-item semi-structured interview across five domains, used in schizophrenia-spectrum research.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Joseph Schear, drawing on Sartre, separates plain experience from self-conscious experience, breaking the link from consciousness to self-consciousness. Marie Guillot distinguishes for-me-ness, me-ishness, and mineness and argues they have been run together. Buddhist reductionists hold that the self is only conventionally real.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The view says little about how for-me-ness relates to neural mechanisms or how far it extends beyond humans.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a description of experience that stays neutral on metaphysics. Zahavi's critique of Dennett's heterophenomenology holds that third-person methods rely on the first-person perspective they claim to replace.

AI_consciousness.rationale: On this view a system would need first-personal givenness, not just the right functions or representations, and Zahavi offers no test for it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Selfhood and meaning are grounded in lived, embodied, interpersonal experience, with no appeal to cosmic purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Copying functional and informational properties would leave out for-me-ness, which Zahavi says such accounts never capture.
